stories.title: Implement WhatsApp MM Lite API with TTL for time-sensitive promotions
stories.description: Meta's Marketing Messages Lite API (MM Lite) enables up to 30% higher delivery rates through AI-optimised delivery, and supports a configurable Time-to-Live (TTL) of 12 hours–30 days so expired flash-sale messages are never delivered late. The existing cost tracker story covers per-message pricing, but no story covers switching the marketing send path to MM Lite or setting TTL per campaign. This matters for Makan Moments daily specials and Pelangi promotional blasts.
acceptanceCriteria: Marketing template sends are routed via MM Lite API endpoint when the mm_lite_enabled flag is true in settings.json
Admin can set a TTL (in hours) per outbound campaign; default is 30 days
Messages not delivered within TTL are marked expired in analytics and never delivered after TTL elapses
A/B delivery benchmark report (delivery rate vs. standard API) is exposed in admin dashboard
technicalNotes: MM Lite API endpoint differs from standard Cloud API; requires separate BSP onboarding and approval
TTL is set at template send time via the ttl field in the API request body, not in WhatsApp Manager only
Reference: https://www.infobip.com/docs/whatsapp/mm-lite
MM Lite is opt-in per WABA; must be enabled before routing traffic to it
dependencies: Update WhatsApp cost tracker for per-message pricing model (July 2025)

stories.title: Webhook message deduplication via Redis idempotency key store
stories.description: WhatsApp Cloud API delivers webhooks at-least-once, meaning duplicate message events are a normal operating condition. Without an idempotency layer, the same inbound guest message can trigger duplicate AI responses or duplicate order entries. This is distinct from the existing 'Persist raw webhook payloads' and 'Complete webhook event routing' stories — those handle storage and routing, not dedup.
acceptanceCriteria: Every inbound webhook event is checked against a Redis key of the form whatsapp:msg:{message_id} before processing
If the key exists, the event is acknowledged with HTTP 200 but skipped; no duplicate AI call is made
Redis keys have a 4-hour TTL to bound memory usage
Deduplication hit count is emitted as a prometheus/log metric
Unit tests cover: first delivery processed, duplicate skipped, TTL expiry causes re-processing
technicalNotes: Use message ID from messages[].id (inbound) or statuses[].id (status updates) as the dedup key
If Redis is unavailable, fall back to in-memory Map with same TTL logic to avoid blocking
Reference: https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/guide-to-whatsapp-webhooks-features-and-best-practices
dependencies: Complete webhook event routing to registered notification handlers

stories.title: Malaysia PDPA 2025: Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) for AI processing
stories.description: Malaysia's PDPA Amendment 2024 (in force from January 2025) and accompanying DPIA Guidelines make a DPIA mandatory when automated AI decision-making affects more than 10,000 data subjects or involves sensitive personal data. Rainbow AI processes guest and customer PII through external LLM providers (NVIDIA, OpenRouter), which constitutes cross-border personal data transfer subject to a Transfer Impact Assessment. This is distinct from the existing DPO and breach-notification stories.
acceptanceCriteria: A DPIA document is created and stored in the admin dashboard covering Rainbow AI's LLM data flows, identifying risks and mitigations
A Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) record is maintained for each external AI provider (NVIDIA, OpenRouter, Ollama cloud) documenting the destination jurisdiction's data protection equivalence
Admin UI displays a DPIA status widget (last reviewed date, next review due within 3 years per CBPDT Guidelines)
System prompt includes a notice that conversations may be processed by an external AI provider, satisfying the data subject notice requirement
technicalNotes: CBPDT Guidelines effective 29 April 2025 require a TIA valid for max 3 years per cross-border transfer mechanism
DPIA is mandatory if AI processes >10,000 data subjects for automated decisions (PDPA Amendment PCP 3/2025)

Reference: https://www.mayerbrown.com/en/insights/publications/2025/07/from-legislative-reform-to-practical-guidance-key-amendments-to-malaysias-pdpa-and-the-launch-of-cross-border-transfer-guidelines
dependencies: Malaysia PDPA 2024 Amendment: DPO appointment and breach notification workflow
Malaysia PDPA 2024 Amendment: PII masking before AI provider API calls

stories.title: Malaysia PDPA 2025: Right to refuse automated AI decisions and request human review
stories.description: Malaysia's PDPA Public Consultation Paper No. 3/2025 on Automated Decision Making and Profiling proposes that individuals have the right to refuse automated outcomes, obtain meaningful explanations, and request human review when AI makes decisions with legal or significant effects. Rainbow AI makes booking suggestions and escalation decisions based on automated profiling. A disclosure and opt-out mechanism is required before finalisation.
acceptanceCriteria: When the AI waiter or hostel assistant makes a recommendation that results in a material action (e.g. order submission, escalation trigger), the user receives a disclosure that the decision was AI-generated
Users can type 'human' or tap a quick-reply button to request human review before any AI-driven action is finalised
An audit log records: decision type, confidence score, whether human review was requested, and outcome
The disclosure message is templated and editable per profile in admin settings
technicalNotes: PCP 3/2025 consultation closed 19 May 2025; final guidelines expected late 2025/early 2026 — implement proactively
Pair with the existing 'Structured chatbot-to-human escalation' story for the handoff mechanics
Reference: https://www.pdp.gov.my/ppdpv1/en/akta/public-consultation-paper-no-3-2025-automated-decision-making-and-profiling-guideline/
dependencies: Structured chatbot-to-human escalation with full conversation context handoff

stories.title: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11: Prevent webchat widget launcher obscuring keyboard focus
stories.description: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Level AA, in force) requires that a focused element is never completely hidden by sticky author-created content. The Rainbow AI webchat widget launcher button (bottom-right fixed position) and any open chat panel are classic failure patterns — they can fully obscure a focused element in the underlying page. The existing 'WCAG 2.1 AA keyboard accessibility' story does not cover this WCAG 2.2-specific criterion.
acceptanceCriteria: When keyboard focus moves to any element on the host page, the floating chat launcher button does not completely obscure that element
When the chat panel is open, tabbing through the page outside the panel does not result in a focused element being entirely hidden behind the panel
The chat panel is dismissible via Escape key without moving focus, so underlying page elements regain visibility
Automated axe-core scan and manual keyboard tab test both pass SC 2.4.11 checks
technicalNotes: Fix options: add scroll-padding-bottom equal to launcher height, or make panel modal (trap focus inside) so underlying page is not navigable while panel is open
SC 2.4.11 only fails on complete obscuration; partial overlap is a 2.4.12 (AAA) concern
Reference: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum
dependencies: WCAG 2.1 AA keyboard accessibility for webchat widget

stories.title: Manglish / code-mixed Malay-English intent normalisation pre-processor
stories.description: Malaysian WhatsApp users routinely write in Manglish — a code-mixed blend of Malay, English, Hokkien, Cantonese, and Tamil slang (e.g. 'nak order nasi lemak 1 la', 'brp harga bilik?'). The existing 'Malay-language ordering' and 'Automatic language detection' stories handle standard Malay and Chinese/Tamil language switching, but not code-mixed informal text that confuses standard NLP intent classifiers. A pre-processor that normalises common Manglish tokens before intent classification would materially improve accuracy.
acceptanceCriteria: A normalisation map of at least 50 common Manglish tokens (e.g. 'brp' to 'berapa', 'nk' to 'nak', 'la/lah/lor' stripped as particles) is maintained in a config file editable via admin UI
The pre-processor runs before the T2 fuzzy-match keyword lookup and LLM intent classification
Intent classification accuracy on a 20-message Manglish test set improves by at least 15% vs. baseline (measured in Vitest semantic tests)
New tokens can be added via admin UI without a code deployment
technicalNotes: Use XLM-RoBERTa or a lightweight transformer fine-tuned on code-mixed SEA data (SeaLLMs-v3) for more robust normalisation beyond a static map
Static map is the pragmatic first step; model-based normalisation can follow in a second iteration
Reference: https://medium.com/mitb-for-all/bridging-the-language-gap-technical-approaches-for-multilingual-ai-in-southeast-asia-f5e52d5dacae
dependencies: Malay-language ordering: AI waiter correctly handles Malay and Manglish order phrases
Automatic language detection and response in Chinese (Mandarin) and Tamil

stories.title: WhatsApp in-chat FPX/DuitNow payment link generation for orders
stories.description: Malaysian guests and cafe customers expect to pay via FPX or DuitNow QR — the dominant local payment methods — without leaving WhatsApp. Meta's per-message pricing model (July 2025) makes the 24-hour service window free, so sending a payment link within a customer-initiated conversation incurs no additional charge. No story currently covers generating a dynamic FPX/DuitNow payment link (via Curlec/Billplz) and sending it as a WhatsApp message with a CTA button.
acceptanceCriteria: After order confirmation, the AI waiter sends a WhatsApp message containing a CTA button linking to a dynamically generated Curlec/Billplz payment page pre-filled with order total and reference
Payment link expires after 30 minutes; a webhook callback from Curlec/Billplz updates the order status to 'paid' in the system
On payment success, the bot sends a utility template message confirming payment received (free within 24h window per July 2025 pricing)
Payment link generation and status updates are logged in the order audit trail
technicalNotes: Curlec (Razorpay Malaysia) supports Payment Links API with FPX, DuitNow QR, and e-wallets
CTA URL button in a WhatsApp template: type 'url', URL = dynamic payment link from Curlec API
Must be sent as a template (not free-form) if outside 24h window; category = 'utility'
dependencies: Order confirmation summary: show itemised receipt before submitting to kitchen
WhatsApp in-chat Webview for mobile payment page

stories.title: WhatsApp Business Calling API: inbound call handling and IVR routing
stories.description: Meta launched the WhatsApp Business Calling API on 15 July 2025, enabling VoIP calls within WhatsApp threads. Unlike the existing 'click-to-call escalation' story (which only covers a button to initiate a call), this story covers the server-side infrastructure needed to receive inbound calls, route them to available staff, and fall back to a voicemail/callback flow when no agent is available.
acceptanceCriteria: Inbound WhatsApp calls to the WABA are received via Cloud API calling webhook and routed to an available agent's WhatsApp number
If no agent is available, an automated voice response (via TTS or pre-recorded audio) informs the caller and offers a callback option
Call events (initiated, answered, ended, missed) are logged in the conversation timeline alongside chat messages
Admin dashboard shows active and missed call metrics per profile
Call permission request template (required before business-initiated calls) is pre-approved and mapped per profile
technicalNotes: Calling API is available for Cloud API only; not available in USA, Canada, Turkey, Egypt, Vietnam, Nigeria as of launch
Business-initiated calls require a prior call-permission template sent within an active thread (max 1 request/24h, 2/7 days)
DTMF keypad support allows simple IVR routing within the call
Reference: https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/calling/
dependencies: WhatsApp Business Calling API: click-to-call escalation button

stories.title: RAG knowledge base staleness detection and automated re-ingestion
stories.description: Rainbow AI uses markdown knowledge base files in .rainbow-kb/ and .rainbow-kb-southern/ that are manually updated. In production, stale KB content causes AI hallucinations where the bot quotes outdated room rates, menu prices, or policies. There is no mechanism to detect when source documents are out of date or alert an admin that re-ingestion is needed. This is distinct from the existing 'LLM response faithfulness check' which validates answers at inference time — this story addresses upstream data freshness.
acceptanceCriteria: Each KB document has a last_verified_at timestamp stored in the rainbow_kb_files table
A configurable staleness threshold (default: 30 days) triggers an alert to the admin WhatsApp when any KB file has not been verified within that period
Admin can mark a KB file as 'verified' via the admin UI, resetting the staleness timer
When a KB file is updated on disk, the system automatically re-ingests (re-embeds) it within 1 hour
Staleness summary is included in the automated daily chatbot performance summary
technicalNotes: Store last_verified_at and last_modified_at in rainbow_kb_files table (already exists per CLAUDE.md)
File watcher (chokidar) or a cron job can detect mtime changes and enqueue re-ingestion
Reference: https://introl.com/blog/rag-infrastructure-production-retrieval-augmented-generation-guide
dependencies: LLM response faithfulness check: flag answers that contradict the knowledge base
Automated daily chatbot performance summary sent to admin via WhatsApp

stories.title: Multi-turn LLM conversation context loss detection and recovery
stories.description: Research (arXiv 2505.06120, 2025) shows LLMs exhibit an average 39% performance drop in multi-turn conversations vs. single-turn. Rainbow AI's context-pruner already summarises old turns, but there is no mechanism to detect mid-conversation context loss (e.g., the bot re-asks already-answered questions or restates the menu). Adding a lightweight context-loss detector that triggers a graceful re-grounding prompt would prevent broken multi-turn ordering and hostel conversations.
acceptanceCriteria: A context-loss heuristic checks each AI response for 3 signals: re-asking already-answered questions, contradicting a prior statement, or omitting a named entity from recent turns
When context loss is detected with confidence > 0.7, the system appends a silent re-grounding message to the next LLM call summarising key facts from the current session
The re-grounding intervention is logged as a 'context_recovery' event in intent_analytics
Vitest tests cover: normal response (no intervention), context-loss detection, re-grounding prompt injection
technicalNotes: Lightweight NLI-based heuristic or prompt-based self-check (cheap model call) can serve as the detector
Integrates with the existing context-pruner.ts — run detection after pruning, before the main LLM call
Reference: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.06120 — 'LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation'

stories.title: CTWA 72-hour free entry point session tracking and cost attribution
stories.description: Under Meta's July 2025 pricing model, conversations initiated through Click-to-WhatsApp (CTWA) ads are free for 72 hours including all message types. The existing 'Click-to-WhatsApp ad referral attribution tracking' story records the referral source but does not track whether the conversation is within the free 72-hour CTWA window or calculate the resulting cost saving. Without this, the billing tracker overcounts costs for CTWA-originated sessions.
acceptanceCriteria: When a CTWA referral webhook is received, the session is tagged with ctwa_entry=true and ctwa_window_expires_at (72h from first message)
The cost tracker skips per-message charges for all messages sent within the CTWA window
Admin dashboard shows CTWA cost savings (estimated cost avoided) as a separate line item
A webhook event is fired when a CTWA window expires, prompting a re-qualification of the conversation type for future billing
technicalNotes: CTWA referral data arrives in the webhook payload under referral.source_type = 'ad'
72-hour window starts from the user's first message, not from ad click; verify with referral.source_id timestamp
Reference: https://www.aichat.com/blog/whatsapp-pricing-update-whats-changing-on-july-1-2025
dependencies: Click-to-WhatsApp ad referral attribution tracking
Update WhatsApp cost tracker for per-message pricing model (July 2025)

stories.title: WhatsApp Flows v4: multi-screen order flow with dynamic menu data
stories.description: WhatsApp Flows v4.0 (released 2025) allows form components to be used without a Form wrapper and supports dynamic screen data retrieved from a live endpoint. No story covers a multi-screen Flows v4 order journey: category selection to item selection with real-time availability to quantity to special instructions to confirmation — all within WhatsApp without leaving the app.
acceptanceCriteria: A WhatsApp Flow with at least 4 screens covers: (1) category selection, (2) item grid with live availability from POS webhook receiver, (3) quantity + special instructions, (4) order summary + submit
Dynamic data endpoint returns current menu availability within 2 seconds; stale data fallback shows cached menu with 'availability may vary' disclaimer
Flow is triggered by a quick-reply button in the AI waiter welcome message
Completed flow payload is parsed server-side and creates an order record identical to the conversational cart flow
Flow JSON validates against WhatsApp Flows v4 schema
technicalNotes: Flows v4.0 components (TextInput, Dropdown, etc.) no longer require Form wrapper — simplifies layout
Use the flows data_exchange endpoint (POST) to serve live menu data per screen
Reference: https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/flows/reference/components/
Encrypted data exchange endpoint required for payment/sensitive screens
dependencies: WhatsApp Flows structured form for table/room reservation
POS webhook receiver: push confirmed orders to kitchen display system
Conversational cart: AI waiter maintains running order across multiple messages

stories.title: PWA service worker background sync for offline webchat message queuing
stories.description: The webchat widget currently fails silently when the user sends a message while offline or on a flaky mobile connection. The Background Sync API (available in all major browsers including iOS 16.4+) allows a service worker to queue outbound messages and retry them when connectivity is restored. This is distinct from the existing 'PWA push notifications for webchat re-engagement' story which covers inbound push — this covers outbound message durability.
acceptanceCriteria: When a user sends a message while offline, it is persisted to IndexedDB and the UI shows 'Message queued — will send when online'
When connectivity is restored, the service worker flushes the queue via the Background Sync API and the message is delivered
If sync fails after 3 retries, the user is notified and can retry manually
The feature works on Chrome, Safari (iOS 16.4+), and Firefox
Vitest/Playwright tests simulate offline state, message queue, and sync on reconnect
technicalNotes: Background Sync API: navigator.serviceWorker.ready.then(sw => sw.sync.register('send-message'))
Store queued messages in IndexedDB (idb library) keyed by a client-generated UUID
Reference: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Progressive_web_apps/Guides/Offline_and_background_operation
dependencies: PWA push notifications for webchat re-engagement on order completion

stories.title: Utility template real-time linter: prevent marketing content in utility templates
stories.description: Meta's July 2025 pricing update tightened the definition of 'utility' templates: any promotional or persuasive element reclassifies the template as 'marketing', doubling the per-message cost. The existing 'WhatsApp template category auto-validator' validates category during submission, but no story provides a real-time guard during template authoring in admin UI that flags suspicious content before submission.
acceptanceCriteria: When an admin authors a template body in the admin UI, a real-time linter highlights phrases that indicate marketing intent (e.g. 'discount', 'offer', 'save X%', 'limited time', 'promocode')
If marketing phrases are detected in a template categorised as 'utility', a warning banner appears before the admin can submit for WhatsApp approval
The linter rules are configurable via a JSON file in admin settings
The guard runs client-side (no server round-trip) using a keyword pattern list
technicalNotes: Regex-based client-side lint; can be enhanced with a cheap LLM call for borderline cases
Reference the July 2025 updated utility definition: non-promotional, not containing promotional or persuasive intent
Reference: https://www.ycloud.com/blog/whatsapp-api-message-template-category-guidelines-update/
dependencies: WhatsApp template category auto-validator: warn on rejection risk before submission

stories.title: Kitchen display system (KDS) outbound order push via REST API
stories.description: Orders placed via the WhatsApp AI waiter or webchat widget currently have a POS webhook receiver for inbound stock sync, but no story covers pushing confirmed orders out to a kitchen display screen in real time. Connecting the AI waiter order confirmation to a KDS closes the loop from guest chat to kitchen prep without manual re-entry.
acceptanceCriteria: When an order is confirmed (post-summary acknowledgment by user), a KDS push request is sent to the configured KDS endpoint within 3 seconds
The KDS push payload includes: order ID, table number, items with quantities, special instructions, and timestamp
If the KDS endpoint is unreachable, the order is queued for retry with exponential backoff (max 3 retries over 2 minutes); admin is alerted on persistent failure
Admin can configure KDS endpoint URL and auth token per profile in admin settings
An order timeline event 'sent to kitchen' is recorded and visible in admin conversation view
technicalNotes: Fresh KDS API: POST /orders with JSON body; reference: https://www.fresh.technology/kds/developer-guide
Local network fallback: Fresh KDS supports on-LAN delivery without internet for offline resilience
This is the outbound complement to the existing 'POS webhook receiver' (inbound stock sync)
dependencies: Order confirmation summary: show itemised receipt before submitting to kitchen
POS webhook receiver: push confirmed orders to kitchen display system

stories.title: WhatsApp delivery receipt pricing_type field ingestion for cost reconciliation
stories.description: Meta's July 2025 pricing update added a new pricing_type sub-field to delivery receipt webhook status events indicating how a delivered message was billed (marketing, utility, authentication, service, or free). The existing cost tracker tallies estimated costs based on template category at send time but cannot reconcile against Meta's actual billed category, which may differ. Ingesting pricing_type from status webhooks enables accurate cost reconciliation.
acceptanceCriteria: The webhook status handler extracts pricing.pricing_type and pricing.billable from delivered message status events
The extracted pricing_type is stored against the message record in rainbow_messages
The cost dashboard shows both estimated cost (from send-time category) and actual billed category (from pricing_type); discrepancies are flagged
A monthly reconciliation report is available in admin UI showing total messages per actual billed category
technicalNotes: pricing_type field is present in the statuses[] array of delivered events as of July 1 2025
Reference: https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/webhooks/reference/messages/status/
A discrepancy between send-time category and pricing_type often indicates a template miscategorisation — auto-flag for admin review
dependencies: Update WhatsApp cost tracker for per-message pricing model (July 2025)

stories.title: Multi-turn LLM evaluation harness with simulated guest conversations
stories.description: Research published in 2025 (Langfuse, OpenEvals) establishes that multi-turn chatbot systems should be evaluated by simulating complete conversations with a user simulator, then scoring the full conversation using LLM-as-a-Judge. Rainbow AI currently has Vitest unit tests for individual tools and Promptfoo for single-turn prompt evals, but no automated harness that simulates a 5-10 turn ordering or check-in conversation end-to-end and scores accuracy, context retention, and task completion.
acceptanceCriteria: A Promptfoo test suite contains at least 10 multi-turn conversation scenarios covering: order placement, order modification, out-of-stock handling, special instruction capture, and hostel check-in
Each scenario is scored on: task_completed (boolean), context_retained (0-1), and hallucination_free (0-1) using an LLM-as-a-Judge evaluator
The harness runs in CI (GitHub Actions) on every PR touching assistant/ or tools/ directories
A regression threshold alerts if average task_completed drops below 0.85 across all scenarios
technicalNotes: Langfuse supports multi-turn simulation via its dataset and experiment features
Promptfoo supports multi-turn test cases with the turns[] array in test case YAML
Reference: https://langfuse.com/blog/2025-10-09-evaluating-multi-turn-conversations
dependencies: Vitest: AI waiter connectivity regression test — POST /api/chat/makan-moments/message must not return error message

stories.title: Admin UI: per-profile WhatsApp message template version history and rollback
stories.description: WhatsApp template approval can take hours to days; a rejected or accidentally broken template causes immediate guest-facing failures. The existing 'Monitor WhatsApp message template quality' story monitors rejection metrics, but no story provides version history and one-click rollback to a previously approved template version in the admin UI.
acceptanceCriteria: Each template in the admin UI shows a version history listing: version number, submission timestamp, approval status, and the template body at that version
An admin can roll back to any previously approved version with a single click; this re-submits the prior body for WhatsApp approval
Version history is stored in rainbow_config_audit (already exists) with template_id as the entity key
The current active version is visually distinguished from pending and rejected versions
technicalNotes: WhatsApp does not support template versioning natively; version history is maintained client-side in rainbow_config_audit
Rollback = create a new template submission via Cloud API with the prior body; the template name may need a suffix increment if Meta rejects re-use of identical names
Reference: https://sanuker.com/guideline-to-whatsapp-template-message-categories/
dependencies: Monitor WhatsApp message template quality and alert on pause/disable
Admin audit log for configuration changes with before/after diff

stories.title: Proactive post-stay WhatsApp review request via utility template
stories.description: Post-stay review solicitation is a proven pattern for hospitality chatbots. Under the July 2025 pricing model, a utility template sent within 24 hours of checkout (as a transaction follow-up) is free within the customer service window. No existing story covers automating a post-checkout review request (Google, Booking.com, or Airbnb) sent via WhatsApp 2-4 hours after checkout, triggered by the check-out event from the POS or booking system.
acceptanceCriteria: A configurable post-checkout delay (default: 2 hours) triggers a WhatsApp utility template message to the guest's JID with a review request link (configurable per profile)
The trigger integrates with the existing POS webhook receiver or can be manually fired from admin UI per booking
If the guest has already rated 4+ stars via in-chat CSAT, the review request is suppressed to avoid duplication
Opt-out guests (tracked by existing opt-out story) never receive the message
Send volume and link click-through rate are tracked in analytics
technicalNotes: Template category = 'utility' (post-transaction follow-up; non-promotional per July 2025 definition)
Schedule via a delayed job queue (e.g. Bull/BullMQ) triggered on checkout event
Review link should be a trackable short URL (UTM-tagged) to measure conversion
dependencies: WhatsApp opt-out tracking and 24-hour compliance processing enforcement
Post-order feedback: AI waiter requests a quick star rating after order is served
POS webhook receiver: push confirmed orders to kitchen display system

stories.title: Structured LLM output schema enforcement with Zod validation and retry
stories.description: Rainbow AI's AI providers return free-form text that is parsed into structured objects (order items, intent classifications, etc.). When the LLM deviates from the expected schema, the current code either silently fails or displays raw JSON to the user (the existing 'Fix raw JSON displayed in chat widget' bug). A systematic solution is to enforce structured output via provider-native JSON mode combined with Zod schema validation and automatic retry with corrective prompting on schema mismatch.
acceptanceCriteria: All LLM calls that expect structured output (intent classification, order extraction, tool call responses) pass a JSON schema to the provider via response_format or equivalent
The response is parsed through the relevant Zod schema; on validation failure, an automatic retry with corrective system message is attempted (max 2 retries)
If all retries fail schema validation, the system falls back to a safe default (e.g. unrecognised intent, ask user to rephrase) rather than propagating raw JSON to the client
Schema validation errors are logged as 'structured_output_failure' events in intent_analytics with provider and model details
Vitest tests cover: valid schema pass, single schema failure with retry success, all retries exhausted fallback
technicalNotes: NVIDIA NIM and OpenRouter support response_format: { type: 'json_object' } and json_schema mode
Zod schemas in src/assistant/schemas.ts are the source of truth — use zodToJsonSchema (zod-to-json-schema package) to generate the provider schema from Zod
Corrective retry prompt: 'Your previous response did not conform to the required JSON schema. Here is the schema: {schema}. Please respond again.'
dependencies: Fix raw JSON displayed in chat widget when LLM returns JSON format
